note: Registry of public transit feeds used by the TRANSIT layer: metro, light rail, tram and bus networks whose operators publish live vehicle data openly for riders. Nothing here is scraped or private. kind: 'positions' = live vehicle coordinates; 'arrivals' = live arrival predictions, where the vehicle is drawn at the stop it is next due at because the feed publishes no vehicle coordinates. mode: rail | bus | tram, which picks the marker and the default colour. Attribution strings are rendered in the UI and must be kept. 'station' = the operator publishes which station a train is at and no coordinates at all; the train is drawn at that station's coordinate from a bundled station list. adapter: oba | tfl | bart | umo | seoul | mbta | digitraffic | opendata-ch | irail | gtfsrt. Static geometry is sourced from operator shapes/stops, connection pass lists/vias, or compact GTFS extracts. For quota-limited feeds pollSec / budgetSec / maxAgeSec are one contract: maxAgeSec >= budgetSec + pollSec and targets × 86400 / budgetSec <= dailyBudget (default 10000), asserted by tests/transit.test.mjs.

feeds.network: Link light rail · Sounder · T Line
feeds.note: Rail routes only (GTFS route types 0/1/2). OneBusAway's public TEST key is documented for API exploration.
One vehicles-for-agency call per refresh; the whole fleet is small enough to poll directly.

feeds.network: Community Transit · Pierce Transit · Everett Transit
feeds.attribution: Community Transit, Pierce Transit & Everett Transit / OneBusAway
feeds.note: King County Metro is deliberately excluded: its vehicles-for-agency payload is over a megabyte per poll, which is too heavy to refresh every minute.

feeds.network: Underground · DLR · Elizabeth line · Overground · Tram
feeds.note: Line colours are Transport for London's official brand colours, stored here so the layer needs no extra request to colour a line. Arrivals are de-duplicated by vehicle id; a train is placed at the station it is next due at.

BART's ETD feed publishes per-station departure predictions with no vehicle ids, so one marker is one departure due within 5 minutes, not one unique train. Uses the demo key BART publishes in its own API documentation. CORS on this host is not guaranteed: the layer tries the browser first and falls back to the /api/fetch relay.

feeds.attribution: Toronto Transit Commission via Umo IQ
feeds.note: Route tags 5xx are TTC streetcars, drawn as trams; everything else is drawn as a bus. CORS on this host is not guaranteed: the layer tries the browser first and falls back to the /api/fetch relay.

feeds.network: Seoul Metropolitan Subway — lines 1–9, Gyeongui–Jungang, Suin–Bundang, Shinbundang, AREX, Ui, Seohae, Sillim
feeds.operator: Seoul Metro · Korail · AREX · Neo Trans · Ui Light Rail
feeds.attribution: Seoul Metropolitan Government open API (실시간 지하철 열차 위치) · station coordinates: Wikidata (CC0)
feeds.note: This is the portal's public sample key, so it is capped at five trains per line: what is drawn is a sample of the fleet, not the whole of it. The endpoint reports which station a train is at, never a position, so each train sits on its station's coordinate and a train at a station the table cannot resolve — or a name shared by two stations, such as 양평 — is not drawn at all. The sample key is limited to 1,000 requests a day for everyone together, so this feed is budgeted, not polled: pollSec / budgetSec / maxAgeSec are one contract (16 lines × 86400/1500 = 921 requests a day at worst, held for 40 minutes so a refused poll never blanks the map) and tests/transit.test.mjs fails if they are retuned apart. The browser makes one bounded relay call for all sixteen lines; the relay's fixed allowlist and per-line cache share each answer for budgetSec, so every visitor shares one request per window instead of spending the key per tab. Register a free key at data.seoul.go.kr and put it in `base` in place of `sample` for full coverage and a larger budget. Korean buses and the metro of Busan, Daegu, Daejeon and Gwangju publish no keyless feed, so they are absent.

feeds.attribution: MBTA V3 API (open data, no key required)
feeds.note: One keyless call returns every vehicle MBTA is running — subway, Green Line, Silver Line and the whole bus fleet — with GPS positions, so this is the layer's densest source. The marker follows the GTFS route type of the route the vehicle is on, so the same feed draws both trains and buses. Positions older than ten minutes are dropped rather than held: a vehicle that stopped reporting is off the map, not frozen on it. Rail line paths and stops load once from MBTA shapes and stops; buses remain live-position-only so the static request stays small.

feeds.network: VR · commuter rail · freight — every train running in Finland
feeds.attribution: Digitraffic / rata.digitraffic.fi — Finnish open railway data (CC 4.0)
feeds.note: Digitraffic publishes every train in the country and which station it has actually reached, but no coordinates, so each train is drawn at that station using the agency's own station table (bundled in `data/fi-stations.json` and refreshed weekly from the agency). The delay shown is the feed's actual time against its scheduled time. A train whose last report is older than fifteen minutes is dropped.

feeds.network: SBB · BLS · PostBus · tram — nationwide departures
feeds.attribution: transport.opendata.ch — Swiss open data timetable (SBB, BLS, PostBus)
feeds.note: Keyless nationwide Swiss departures with the live delay, one board per hub re-read every five minutes, and at most three departures drawn per station so the map stays readable. Departures that have already left are dropped; a marker is a scheduled departure at the station it leaves from, not a GPS position. Static network paths use the operator connection journey passList coordinates; station dots come from those same published timetable points.

iRail republishes SNCB/NMBS departure boards as open data with no key: delay in seconds, platform and station coordinates. Cancelled and already-departed services are dropped. Twelve hubs re-read every six minutes. Static lines use iRail connection vias and station dots use iRail’s published station list.

GTFS-Realtime is the format most of the world's bus agencies publish, so the layer carries a small protobuf reader for it rather than a per-agency adapter: any agency that publishes a keyless VehiclePositions URL can be added here with adapter "gtfsrt" and no new code. Positions are the agency's own; ones older than ten minutes are dropped. The bundled static GTFS extract supplies line geometry and station dots; its refresh workflow only retains public routes, shapes and stops.

retired.reason: gtfs.gcrta.org stopped answering entirely — unreachable over both http and https on two sweeps (09:34Z and 09:53Z) and on a direct check. The feed is not polled while it is retired; the bundled static geometry in data/gcrta-static.json is kept because it is still the reference for what this reader was built against.

feeds.network: DTC & cluster buses — every GPS-fitted bus in Delhi
feeds.operator: Delhi Transport Corporation · DIMTS (via Open Transit Data, Government of NCT of Delhi)
feeds.attribution: Open Transit Data — Government of NCT of Delhi (otd.delhi.gov.in)
feeds.signup: otd.delhi.gov.in — free registration, key is emailed
feeds.note: Delhi's Open Transit Data portal is India's only public live transit feed: real bus GPS updated roughly every ten seconds as GTFS-Realtime VehiclePositions — no TripUpdates feed exists. A registered key is already in place (free from otd.delhi.gov.in; keep it rotated if the deployed site is public). keyEnv names the server-side environment variable the relay publishes the key from: set DELHI_OTD_KEY in the Netlify project (Functions scope) or the local environment and the layer uses that value instead of the key in this public file, which should then be treated as exposed and rotated at otd.delhi.gov.in. Buses that stop reporting — parked at a depot for hours — stay visible for up to thirty minutes and fade as their report ages; anything older is dropped rather than drawn as if live. The same portal's DMRC area publishes only static timetable data: the Delhi Metro itself publishes no real-time train feed anywhere, and no train marker may be drawn for it until DMRC chooses to (their November 2025 MapmyIndia MoU is a closed commercial channel, not open data). Never substitute simulated trains for that feed.

The same Trapeze GTFS-Realtime endpoint family as Cleveland's GCRTA feed, keyless and verified live: real bus GPS across Fulton, DeKalb and Clayton counties. MARTA rail positions are not part of this VehiclePositions feed, so only buses are drawn — no train marker is invented.

feeds.network: ETS buses & LRT trains — every vehicle reporting
feeds.operator: Edmonton Transit Service · City of Edmonton
feeds.attribution: City of Edmonton open data — GTFS-Realtime (no key)
feeds.note: City of Edmonton's open-data GTFS-Realtime endpoint, same Trapeze endpoint family as Cleveland, keyless and verified live ahead of registration: every reporting ETS vehicle, buses and LRT alike, drawn from the agency's own GPS stream.

feeds.network: Qbuzz · RET · GVB · Connexxion · Arriva · EBS · HTM — nationwide bus, tram & metro
feeds.operator: All Dutch public transport operators (via OVapi)
feeds.note: One national keyless GTFS-Realtime feed carries every Dutch bus, tram and metro reporting — thousands of vehicles from every operator at once, so the budget is doubled to spare a big binary payload and the layer draws the ones nearest the view. NS rail trains are not drawn: OVapi's trainUpdates feed uses a non-standard protobuf extension this reader deliberately does not guess at, and no train is ever placed without a real position.

feeds.attribution: Open Government Data Malaysia — data.gov.my GTFS-Realtime (no key)
feeds.note: Malaysia's official open-data portal publishes keyless GTFS-Realtime vehicle positions for Rapid KL buses — real GPS with fleet plates, round-numbered against the agency's own updates. Some buses report sparsely outside peak hours, so a bus stays on the map for up to thirty minutes and fades as its report ages instead of flickering out. Rail agencies on the portal publish trip updates but no vehicle positions, so no KL train markers are drawn. Measured on 2026-09-29: the endpoint answers a well-formed feed (15 bytes, header only) but has published no vehicle entities in two sweeps — the operator's own stream is empty, which the chip reports as 'answered with no vehicle entities' rather than as a fault.

feeds.network: HSL buses, trams and metro — Helsinki region
feeds.note: Keyless GTFS-Realtime VehiclePositions for the whole HSL network — bus, tram and metro together, which is why this one feed carries more vehicles than most registries do networks. Measured 913 drawable vehicles when it was promoted on 2026-09-29. Finland’s rail positions arrive separately through the Digitraffic feed (fi-rail); nothing here is interpolated.

Keyless VehiclePositions straight from the operator, no portal or key involved. Measured 391 drawable vehicles when it was promoted on 2026-09-29 — a full city fleet, not a sample. Intermittent: the same URL answered 404 on two later sweeps that morning and on a direct check, so this endpoint comes and goes — the chip reports it per sweep instead of the registry pretending it is always there.

feeds.operator: Capital Metro (via the Texas open data portal)
feeds.attribution: Capital Metro / Texas Department of Transportation open data portal
feeds.note: The operator’s realtime feed republished by the state open-data portal, so the endpoint is a download URL rather than an API path — it answers with the same GTFS-Realtime bytes. Measured 272 drawable vehicles when it was promoted on 2026-09-29.

CTtransit was recorded as dead in this registry and left out for that reason; probed on 2026-09-29 it answered with 224 drawable vehicles from this endpoint, so it is back in. The registry’s rule stands either way: a network is listed only while its own feed answers, and the weekly probe is what keeps that true.

feeds.operator: Hamilton Street Railway (City of Hamilton open data)
feeds.attribution: City of Hamilton open data — GTFS-Realtime
feeds.note: A municipal open-data endpoint with no key and no signup. Measured 133 drawable vehicles when it was promoted on 2026-09-29.

feeds.network: Broward County Transit buses — Fort Lauderdale
feeds.attribution: Broward County Transit GTFS-Realtime (public feed, no key)
feeds.note: Keyless county feed. Measured 110 drawable vehicles when it was promoted on 2026-09-29.

The operator publishes its VehiclePositions file into an S3 bucket rather than an API host, which is why the endpoint is not the operator’s own domain — it is the feed the Mobility Database catalog lists for them. Measured 62 drawable vehicles when it was promoted on 2026-09-29. Intermittent: the object it publishes returned NoSuchKey on two later sweeps that morning and on a direct check, so it is absent much of the time — reported per sweep, never assumed live.

feeds.network: ACTV buses and water buses — Venice
feeds.note: Keyless operator feed covering the road fleet and the lagoon water buses. Measured 50 drawable vehicles when it was promoted on 2026-09-29.

A small regional operator publishing keyless VehiclePositions from its own host. Measured 30 drawable vehicles when it was promoted on 2026-09-29; the city is recorded as the region because the catalog lists no municipality for it.

feeds.network: Greater Portland Metro buses — Portland, Maine
feeds.attribution: Greater Portland Metro GTFS-Realtime (public feed, no key)
feeds.note: Portland, Maine — not Portland, Oregon, which publishes no keyless vehicle feed. Measured 10 drawable vehicles when it was promoted on 2026-09-29. Intermittent: this host answered 503 on two later sweeps that morning and on a direct check — reported per sweep, and the smallest fleet in the registry (10 buses measured).

feeds.attribution: Guelph Transit GTFS-Realtime (public feed, no key)
feeds.note: Keyless municipal feed. Measured 33 drawable vehicles when it was promoted on 2026-09-29.
